cards.text: God just spoke from the mountain, and the people were so scared they stood at a distance while Moses, Israel's leader, went into the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:18-21). Now the LORD gives Moses a message for the Israelites. It opens with something they've seen for themselves.

cards.question: God reminds the Israelites they've seen for themselves that He spoke to them. Where did He speak from?
God has spoken to them straight from heaven. Next, what does He say they must not make for themselves?

answers.text: a king to rule over them
a tower that reaches the sky

cards.text: What they ARE to make is an altar of earth for their burnt offerings and peace offerings. DIRT, friend, and as a stamper who came out of a clearance bin for a quarter, that's my kind of building project.

cards.question: In every place where God causes His name to be remembered, He promises to come to them and ___ them.
If they build the altar out of stones instead, God wants those stones carefully cut and shaped with tools.

cards.text: One more altar rule: no going up to God's altar on steps, so nobody's nakedness is exposed on it. Friend, I wear a full apron just to stamp COOKIES, so you won't hear me argue with that one.

Then the LORD gives Moses ordinances for everyday life: how to treat servants, what's owed when someone gets hurt or an ox gores, and how to care for foreigners, widows, orphans and the poor. There's even a rule to help the donkey of someone who hates you when it falls under its load, plus the famous line “eye for eye, tooth for tooth.” Three chapters of rules, and not ONE about sneaking cookie dough off the counter. I looked.

cards.question: After all those laws, God tells them to pay close attention to everything He's said. Then what must never be heard on their lips?

cards.text: Last come the feasts: three times a year they celebrate a feast to God, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Harvest and the Feast of Ingathering. Keep your apron on, friend, because this conversation isn't finished.
